newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends sharply up on charts, US supplies - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends sharply up on charts, US supplies - Jan 23.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended sharply higher on Thursday after another round of U.S. inventory reports painted a tighter picture for distillate inventories, traders said.
A technical correction was also in the cards, they said, after prices lost close to $30 a tonne, or 13 percent, in the last two weeks and it held the psychological $200 mark the previous two days.
But crude oil prices trimmed some of their gains late in the session after the March contract failed to crack an upside gap that served as resistance.
Feb gas oil settled $5.00 higher at $208.00 a tonne and the Feb/Mar spread widened by about $1.00, a sign of near-term strength ahead of Feb's expiry next month.
"I think it's a combination of the APIs and DOEs," said Tony Machacek, an oil broker at Credit Lyonnais Rouse.
"A general recovery in prices is due after the recent falls that we've seen...Even the specs who are short must start to question how much further it can go to the downside," he said.
American Petroleum Institute said late Wednesday distillates fell 3.0 million barrels. Today's Energy Information Administration report added more fuel to the fire.
At 1757 GMT, March Brent was up 24 cents at $22.72 a barrel after hitting a session high $22.90, just below the start of the gap at $22.94.
The EIA also registered a smaller weekly decline in crude inventories than the API report, 1.5 million versus 3.4 million.

Machacek said crude's momentum appeared to be running out after the early rally. He put resistance at $23 and support at $22.60, a previous downtrend line off its recent highs that was broken earlier.
